COMPONENT KIT

  • SDF lens — a circular refraction pass (or a scaled DOM copy) magnifying what sits under it
  • Metal barrel — conic-gradient ring and handle that make it a physical instrument
  • Dispersion — red/cyan channel offset on everything seen through the glass
  • Fresnel rim — bright edge band + faint coral/ink fringe at the lens border
  • Hidden ink — coral marks that only render inside the lens mask — the anomaly
  • Hanging tag — mono readout on a leader line off the loupe: time + deploy

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Lens glide — bezier path, sine.inOut 3 s = 6 beats; each row or card crossing lands on a beat
  • Magnify settle — scale 1 → 1.8, expo.out 0.3 s, triggered on a downbeat when the lens stops
  • Dispersion spike — RGB split 0 → 8 px → 0 over 3 frames on the snare when the anomaly is found

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

“The lens that sees what you missed” is the whole product promise in one precise, premium image, and the calm table outside the glass makes the coral inside unmistakable. Risk: a real refraction pass needs WebGL and a pre-baked table texture; the DOM-copy fallback must match the table exactly.

Adapt to your product: Lay your product's densest real screen (a log, a list, a table) flat and let the loupe find the one row your product flags; the hidden-ink trick works for any “we noticed this” feature.

References: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2026/09/08/building-an-infinite-liquid-glass-grid-with-three-js-webgpu-and-tsl/ (refractive glass over a grid in WebGPU) · https://github.com/ybouane/liquidglass (DOM liquid-glass refraction library)
